report: The image displays mixed renal cell carcinoma, featuring clear cell RCC on the left with clear cytoplasm and well-defined borders, and chromophobe RCC on the right with eosinophilic cytoplasm and irregular nuclei. The clear cells are polygonal with a vascular network, while the chromophobe cells are larger with a reticular pattern. No significant necrosis or inflammation is observed.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma histology
evidence.text: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma can show lepidic, acinar, papillary, micropapillary, or solid growth with mucin, and mixed patterns are common. Squamous differentiation is supported morphologically by keratinization, keratin pearl formation, and intercellular bridges. Poorly differentiated tumors may require immunohistochemistry.

evidence.title: Decision tree for pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features versus metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma
evidence.text: A decision tree using TTF-1, SATB2, CDX2, and CK7 was developed to distinguish primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features from metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. The validation results support using multiple markers and clinical context when assigning a primary site.

review.assessment: The case describes a mixed renal cell carcinoma containing both clear cell and chromophobe components, which aligns with the 'kidney renal clear cell carcinoma' candidate label, although the report indicates a mixed morphology.
rationale: The de-identified report explicitly identifies 'clear cell RCC' with 'clear cytoplasm and well-defined borders', matching the case-specific prompt for kidney renal clear cell carcinoma.
The report describes a 'vascular network', which corresponds to the 'chicken-wire vasculature' characteristic of clear cell RCC.
CONCH and PLIP (baseline) and MUSK (prompted) correctly identified the kidney renal clear cell carcinoma label.
discrepancies: The report identifies a mixed tumor (clear cell and chromophobe RCC), but the candidate labels only provide a specific option for clear cell RCC.
MUSK (baseline), PLIP (prompted), and QUILTNET (both) incorrectly suggested lung or glioma labels.
recommended_review: Pathologist review to confirm the proportion of chromophobe vs. clear cell components as the candidate labels do not allow for 'mixed RCC'.
limitations: Retrieved literature focused on lung and skin cancers and provided no evidence regarding renal cell carcinoma morphology.
Candidate labels are mutually exclusive and do not account for mixed histological subtypes.
